documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 54 yo M, transferring care; his old PCP retired. Drives long-haul, gone 4-5 days at a stretch, prefers portal and video when he is on the road.

PMH: kidney transplant March 2018 at an outside transplant center, followed there yearly, graft has been stable per patient (baseline creatinine around 1.2). HTN for years, on amlodipine and HCTZ. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin. Peptic ulcer years ago, no details, no bleeding he knows of. COPD, mild, told so after breathing tests a few years back, uses albuterol maybe once a month, needs a new inhaler. Both knees ache, worse after long runs; takes OTC naproxen 220 mg twice a day when they act up.
PSH: kidney transplant 2018.
Meds: tacrolimus 5 mg BID and prednisone 5 mg daily (transplant team writes these), amlodipine 10 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, naproxen sodium 220 mg BID prn, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had an MI at 62 (CAD). Mother with high blood pressure. Maternal uncle on dialysis, cause never known.
SH: single, lives alone in an apartment in town. Smokes about half a pack a day, ~25 pack-years. Not ready to quit cold, would like to cut down in steps. Alcohol a drink or two a month. Runs long distances, several races a year.

ROS negative except knees.
Exam: BP as charted. Well-appearing, lean. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze, good air movement. Abdomen soft; well-healed right lower quadrant transplant incision, graft nontender. Knees: crepitus both, no effusion. No edema. Skin: no lesions.

A/P
1. Kidney transplant, stable per history. Immunosuppression per transplant center. Requesting their records and our prior office's.
2. HTN, near goal. Continue amlodipine/HCTZ.
3. Hyperlipidemia, continue atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
4. Tobacco: gradual-reduction plan - drop 2-3 cigarettes a week, pick a quit date once he's under 5 a day. Will check in by video in ~3 months.
5. COPD, mild by hx: albuterol refilled.
6. Knee OA: using naproxen sparingly per pt.
7. HM: flu and Tdap today. Records will tell us colonoscopy status.
Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, Mg, UA.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Charles, your labs look good. Kidney function is right where the transplant records say your baseline sits, blood counts and liver tests are normal, A1c is normal, and urine shows no protein. LDL is 120 on the atorvastatin, which we'll keep an eye on. Talk soon.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care and transplant center
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Records received and reviewed (58 pages).

Prior PCP: HTN since early 2010s, hyperlipidemia, knee OA. Remote peptic ulcer noted in history only. COPD noted after spirometry in 2016, mild. Smoker throughout. Colonoscopy 2017 as part of transplant evaluation: normal, repeat in 10 years.

Transplant center: kidney transplant 03/2018, uncomplicated course. Native kidney disease cause not established. Hepatitis C antibody and HIV screen negative during evaluation. Maintenance tacrolimus and prednisone; tacrolimus troughs in range on recent checks. Graft creatinine 1.1-1.3 since 2019.

Nothing here changes our plan. Colonoscopy next due 2027.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology annual visit
documents.author: transplant nephrology
documents.body:
Transplant Nephrology Clinic
Visit date: 10/14/2020

Dear colleague,
Thank you for taking over primary care for Mr. Moran, now 2.5 years after his kidney transplant. He feels well. Graft function is stable with a creatinine of 1.2, no proteinuria, and his tacrolimus trough is within our target range. Blood pressure in clinic 136/82.

Immunosuppression unchanged: tacrolimus 5 mg twice daily, prednisone 5 mg daily. We will continue to prescribe both. Please avoid live vaccines.

Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up here in one year with labs every 3 months through our lab.

Sincerely,
Transplant Nephrology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 56 yo M. Feels well; still smoke-free since May. Ran a half marathon in October. Knees grumble afterward, naproxen a couple days, then fine.
Meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, prednisone 5, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, naproxen 220 prn, albuterol prn (hasn't needed it since summer). NKDA.
ROS: no chest pain, breathing good, no GI symptoms, no urinary complaints, mood good.
Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abd soft, graft site nontender. Prostate deferred. Joints - knee crepitus, full ROM. Skin without suspicious lesions, some sun-weathering on L forearm from the truck window. No edema.

A/P
- Health maintenance: flu and PCV20 today. Colonoscopy 2017 normal, due 2027. Shingrix done, COVID x3 done. PSA after discussion - he wanted it, drawn today.
- Lung cancer screening: new 2021 criteria now include him (age 56, 25 pk-yr, quit <15 yr). Low-dose CT ordered; scheduling will call him.
- HTN, lipids, transplant - labs today; continue current regimen.
- Sun protection on the driving arm.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Charles - all of this year's labs are fine, including the PSA. Kidney numbers steady. Imaging scheduling will reach out about the screening CT.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine visit. No complaints today. Taking everything as prescribed.

He signed up this spring for a long-term research study looking at diet and heart disease (questionnaires and food diaries, no study drug). The study team shared that people eating more fiber seemed to have fewer heart problems, so he has switched to oatmeal most mornings and packs vegetables for the road. Asked whether he should trust that. We talked about why an early finding from an observational study can be explained by other habits that go along with eating fiber (fiber eaters also tend to exercise more, smoke less), and that more fiber is a good idea for him either way.

Still not smoking, a year now. Running 3-4 days a week.
Meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, prednisone 5, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, naproxen 220 prn, albuterol prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 132/84. Comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Exam otherwise unremarkable.

Labs from 5/24 (fasting): TC 190, HDL 40, LDL 120, TG 150, fasting glucose 96, A1c 5.6.

A/P
- HTN at goal on current two drugs.
- Lipids stable on atorvastatin 40, no change.
- A1c normal on chronic prednisone.
- Lung screening CT still not done - he says he'll book it on his next stretch home.
- Recheck in ~6 months, physical in the fall.

documents.title: Headaches and BP
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Been getting headaches most days and a few dizzy spells when I stand up from the cab. Checked my pressure at a truck stop machine and on my cuff, getting 150s and 160s over high 90s. Taking my pills. Transplant clinic appointment isn't until October. What should I do?

documents.title: RE: Headaches and BP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. With your transplant, a new jump in blood pressure is something your kidney team should look at soon. I called their office this morning and they are moving your visit up to later this month; they will call you with the date. Keep taking your medicines and keep a log. If you get a severe headache, chest pain, weakness, trouble speaking or vision changes, go to the ER.

documents.title: Call to transplant nephrology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with the transplant nephrology nurse re: new elevated home BPs 150-160s/high 90s with headaches. They will see him in clinic on 8/26. Pt notified via portal.

events.reason: Headaches, dizziness and elevated blood pressure

conditions.label: Secondary hypertension due to renal artery stenosis

documents.title: Transplant nephrology clinic note
documents.author: transplant nephrology
documents.body:
Transplant Nephrology Clinic
Date of visit: 08/26/2022
Referring: primary care

History: Mr. Moran, kidney transplant 2018, seen at the request of his primary care physician (last primary care visit in May). He describes headaches and episodes of lightheadedness going back roughly six months, which he had put down to long driving shifts. Home and kiosk readings have climbed into the 150s-160s systolic. He reports taking amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide daily and has been keeping salt down.

Current medications: tacrolimus 5 mg twice daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, naproxen sodium 220 mg twice daily as needed, albuterol as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, quit last year; drives long-haul.

Exam: BP 162/98 seated, repeated. Heart regular. A bruit with both systolic and diastolic components is heard over the epigastrium. Peripheral pulses equal and symmetric. No JVD, lungs clear, no edema, no other sign of heart failure.

Labs today: creatinine 1.2, at his baseline; renal function otherwise normal.

Assessment: new resistant hypertension with a bruit in a transplant recipient, concerning for renal artery stenosis. Secondary hypertension due to renal artery stenosis.
Plan: Doppler ultrasound of the transplant kidney and its artery next week. Continue current antihypertensives meanwhile. If stenosis is confirmed we will refer to interventional radiology.

Transplant Nephrology

reports.text:
EXAM: Ultrasound of the transplant kidney with color and spectral Doppler.
INDICATION: Resistant hypertension, abdominal bruit, kidney transplant 2018.
FINDINGS: Right iliac fossa transplant kidney measures 11.6 cm, normal in size with normal cortical echogenicity. No hydronephrosis. No perinephric collection. Transplant renal vein patent. At the arterial anastomosis the peak systolic velocity is 310 cm/s with aliasing, and intrarenal arterial waveforms downstream are tardus-parvus in appearance.
IMPRESSION: Findings consistent with significant stenosis of the transplant renal artery at the anastomosis. Otherwise normal transplant kidney.
reports.conclusion: Significant transplant renal artery stenosis at the anastomosis (PSV 310 cm/s).

documents.title: Outside imaging received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Doppler shows transplant renal artery stenosis. Transplant nephrology has referred him to IR. Message sent to pt.

documents.title: Transplant renal artery angioplasty and stent
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Interventional Radiology Procedure Report
Date of procedure: 09/27/2022

Procedure: Transplant renal arteriogram, balloon angioplasty and stent placement.
Indication: Hemodynamically significant transplant renal artery stenosis on Doppler with resistant hypertension.
Allergies: NKDA.
Access: Left common femoral artery, ultrasound guided. Moderate sedation.
Findings: Focal high-grade stenosis just beyond the anastomosis of the transplant renal artery. Kidney perfuses well beyond it.
Intervention: Angioplasty followed by a balloon-expandable stent. Completion angiogram shows brisk flow with no residual narrowing and no dissection. Low contrast volume used.
Hemostasis with closure device. No complications.
Disposition: Observed and discharged home the same afternoon. Creatinine check in 1 week via transplant lab. Antihypertensives unchanged for now; transplant nephrology to follow pressures.

events.reason: Follow-up after renal artery stent; vaccines

Here 3 wks after transplant renal artery stent. Headaches gone within days; no more dizzy spells. Home readings 120s/70s-80s. Groin site healed.

BP today 128/80.

orders.reason: Right upper lobe mass on X-ray
Right upper lobe lung mass, urgent

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: cough x 2 wks, weight down.
HPI: dry cough, started late Oct, not getting better. Scale shows about 5 lb lost over the last month without trying; he hadn't changed his running. No fever, sweats or blood in sputum. No chest pain. Mild extra breathlessness on hills. Never did the screening CT.
PMH: kidney tx on tacrolimus/prednisone, COPD mild, former smoker 25 pk-yr quit 5/2021.
Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile, sat normal. Weight down from summer. Lungs: breath sounds slightly diminished over the right upper chest, no crackles, no wheeze. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Heart RRR.
CXR today: ~2 cm RUL mass.
A/P: RUL lung mass in a former heavy smoker with weight loss - concerning for malignancy. CT chest ordered this week; urgent pulmonology referral placed. Discussed with him frankly; he understands. Cancelled the old screening order since he'll have a diagnostic CT. Notified transplant team.

reports.text:
EXAM: CT chest without contrast.
INDICATION: Right upper lobe mass on radiograph.
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph 11/07/2022.
FINDINGS: Solid mass in the right upper lobe measuring 2.0 x 1.8 cm in axial dimensions. No hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion. No other pulmonary nodules. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. Osseous structures intact.
IMPRESSION: 2.0 cm solid right upper lobe mass without lymphadenopathy, suspicious for primary lung malignancy. Tissue sampling recommended.
reports.conclusion: 2.0 cm right upper lobe mass, no lymphadenopathy.

documents.title: CT result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CT result: mass confirmed, about 2 cm, no enlarged lymph nodes. Pulmonology appt 11/25. He asked if it could be anything but cancer - told him it could, but the biopsy will tell us, and that no enlarged nodes is good news. He'll be off the road that week.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonary Medicine Consultation
Date of service: 11/25/2022
Reason: right upper lobe mass

HPI: 57-year-old man, kidney transplant recipient on tacrolimus and prednisone, seen by transplant nephrology in August, with COPD and a 25 pack-year smoking history (stopped about 18 months ago). Over the last month he has developed a new cough and has lost about five pounds. He denies fevers, night sweats and coughing up blood.
Meds: tacrolimus, prednisone, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, naproxen as needed, albuterol as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: long-haul truck driver; alcohol 1-2 drinks a month.
Family: father with CAD.

Exam: Vital signs normal. Breath sounds are reduced over the right upper lobe; no wheezes or crackles. No lymphadenopathy. Cardiac exam normal. No clubbing.

Imaging reviewed: chest radiograph 11/07 with a 2 cm right upper lobe mass; CT chest 11/10 confirming a 2.0 cm solid mass with no lymph node enlargement.

Assessment: solitary 2 cm right upper lobe mass in a former smoker, high suspicion for primary lung cancer, radiographically node-negative.
Plan:
1. CT-guided needle biopsy, scheduled 12/01.
2. Full pulmonary function testing with DLCO.
3. PET-CT for staging.
4. Referral to thoracic surgery once tissue diagnosis is back.
Will send results to primary care.

Pulmonary Medicine

documents.title: CT-guided right upper lobe lung biopsy
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Procedure: CT-guided percutaneous core needle biopsy, right upper lobe mass.
Date: 12/01/2022
Allergies: NKDA.
Posterior approach, patient prone. Local anesthesia and moderate sedation. 19-gauge coaxial needle advanced to the 2.0 cm mass; four 20-gauge cores obtained and sent to pathology.
Post-procedure CT and 2-hour chest film: no pneumothorax. No hemoptysis.
Discharged home with precautions.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: Right upper lobe, 2 cm, non-small cell

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Lung, right upper lobe mass, CT-guided core needle biopsy.
GROSS: Four tan cores, 0.8 to 1.4 cm, entirely submitted.
MICROSCOPIC: Cores contain infiltrating malignant epithelial cells forming nests and irregular glands within desmoplastic stroma. No small cell features.
DIAGNOSIS: Non-small cell lung carcinoma.
Note: Results discussed with the ordering pulmonologist.
reports.conclusion: Non-small cell lung carcinoma, right upper lobe.

documents.title: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonology called pt yesterday with biopsy: non-small cell lung cancer. I called him this morning to check in. He's shaken but practical, wants to know next steps. Staging PET and PFTs scheduled next week, then thoracic surgery. Offered a video visit to talk it through - booked for 12/16. Lung cancer added to problem list.

reports.text:
Pulmonary function testing: spirometry, lung volumes and DLCO.
Effort and reproducibility acceptable.
FEV1/FVC 0.66. FEV1 81% predicted. FVC within normal limits. No significant bronchodilator response. Lung volumes normal. DLCO 76% predicted.
INTERPRETATION: Mild obstructive ventilatory defect. Mildly reduced diffusing capacity. Values support tolerance of lobectomy.

events.reason: Right upper lobe non-small cell lung cancer

documents.title: Thoracic surgery consultation
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Thoracic Surgery Consultation
Date: 12/14/2022

Mr. Moran is a 57-year-old former smoker and kidney transplant recipient with a 2.0 cm right upper lobe mass; core biopsy 12/01 shows non-small cell carcinoma.

Staging: PET-CT 12/12 shows FDG uptake in the right upper lobe mass only, with no hilar, mediastinal or distant uptake. Clinical stage IA (cT1b N0 M0).
PFTs 12/08: FEV1 81%, DLCO 76% predicted.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications per primary care list.

Exam: well, active, runs regularly. Lungs with reduced breath sounds right apex. Heart regular.

Recommendation: video-assisted thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Risks and benefits reviewed; he wishes to proceed. Transplant nephrology aware; stress-dose steroids per anesthesia. Surgery scheduled 01/10/2023.

Thoracic Surgery

Video, pt at home.

events.reason: Right upper lobectomy for lung cancer

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: A. Lung, right upper lobe, lobectomy. B-E. Mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes (stations 2R, 4R, 7, 10R, 11R).
GROSS: Right upper lobe, 15.5 x 9.0 x 4.0 cm. A firm tan-white mass, 2.0 cm in greatest dimension, lies 2.5 cm from the bronchial margin and does not pucker the pleura.
MICROSCOPIC: Invasive adenocarcinoma. Visceral pleura not involved. No lymphovascular invasion identified.
MARGINS: Bronchial, vascular and parenchymal margins negative.
LYMPH NODES: 0 of 9 lymph nodes involved.
PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT1b N0 (AJCC 8th edition), stage IA2.
reports.conclusion: Invasive adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe, 2.0 cm, margins negative, 0/9 nodes, pT1b N0, stage IA2.

documents.title: Thoracic surgery discharge summary
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Discharge Summary - Thoracic Surgery
Admitted: 01/10/2023  Discharged: 01/13/2023

Procedure 01/10: video-assisted thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Uncomplicated. Single chest tube removed postoperative day 2 after air leak resolved. Stress-dose hydrocortisone given perioperatively and tapered back to his home prednisone by discharge. Tacrolimus continued with levels checked by the transplant team; creatinine stable at baseline.

Final pathology: invasive adenocarcinoma, 2.0 cm, all margins negative, 0 of 9 nodes, pT1b N0, stage IA2.

Condition at discharge: ambulating independently, room air saturations normal, pain controlled.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: home medications unchanged (tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, albuterol as needed). Naproxen held for now.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb or driving for 2 weeks; walking daily. Thoracic surgery clinic in 2-3 weeks; oncology to review pathology. PCP follow-up in 1-2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
10 days post VATS RUL lobectomy. Walking 2 miles a day. Some soreness at the port sites and along the right side, settling. The cough he had before surgery is fading. No fever, no sputum, no leg swelling. Appetite back.
Path came back stage IA2 adenocarcinoma, nodes negative - surgeon and oncology going over it with him next month.
Meds: home regimen, has not restarted naproxen.
Exam: afebrile, sat normal on RA. Incisions clean and dry, no erythema. Breath sounds slightly reduced R apex, no crackles. Calves soft.
A/P: recovering well. Pathology reviewed with him. Keep walking. Oncology and surgery f/u scheduled. Return to driving cleared by surgery on their timeline.

documents.title: Thoracic oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Thoracic Oncology
Visit date: 02/15/2023

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Moran after his right upper lobectomy for a 2.0 cm adenocarcinoma, pT1b N0, stage IA2, with negative margins. He has recovered well and is back to walking and light jogging.

For completely resected stage IA disease, adjuvant systemic therapy is not recommended, and he agrees. Plan surveillance CT chest every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly. Next scan July 2023.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: per your list; tacrolimus and prednisone per transplant.

Thank you for involving us.
Thoracic Oncology

documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body: Postoperative visit 02/01/2023: incisions healed, lungs expanding well on chest film, no air or fluid. Cleared to drive and return to work 2/13. Can resume running gradually. Discharged from surgical follow-up; surveillance with oncology.

Routine f/u. Back to full-time driving since February and running 3 days a week, about 10-12 miles total. Breathing fine. Weight coming back.

He brought a printout about a research trial of a new cholesterol drug that is recruiting people with high LDL and asked if he should sign up. Told him he's welcome to call the study line, though his transplant medicines and recent cancer surgery may keep him out. He's not sure he wants the extra visits with his schedule. Not enrolled.

58-year-old man, kidney transplant 2018 on tacrolimus and prednisone, referred by primary care for a non-healing ulcer of the right forearm that has been enlarging over roughly three months. No fever, weight loss or night sweats.
History also notable for resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma (1/2023).
Medications: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, naproxen 220 mg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: right dorsal forearm, 2.0 cm ulcer with raised, everted margins and a central keratin-filled core. No regional lymphadenopathy (epitrochlear, axillary). Full skin examination otherwise unremarkable.

Recent labs (11/13): Hgb 13.2, WBC 7,500, platelets 250,000; creatinine 1.4, BUN 18, ALT 25, AST 30.
Chest X-ray obtained today given immunosuppression and cancer history: no evidence of metastatic disease.

Procedure: after informed consent and local lidocaine, deep shave biopsy of the ulcer edge. Hemostasis with aluminum chloride. Specimen to dermatopathology.

Impression: clinically squamous cell carcinoma. Will arrange Mohs surgery once pathology confirms.
Dermatology

conditions.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of skin of right upper limb

SPECIMEN: Skin, right forearm, deep shave biopsy.
MICROSCOPIC: Atypical keratinocytes in nests and strands invading the dermis, with keratin pearl formation. Well differentiated. Tumor extends to the deep and peripheral margins of the biopsy.
DIAGNOSIS: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, well differentiated.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy
Date: 11/29/2024
Indication: hematemesis and melena.
Allergies: NKDA. Moderate sedation.
Findings: Esophagus normal. Stomach with a small amount of old blood, mucosa otherwise normal; biopsies of antrum and body for H. pylori. Duodenal bulb: 1.5 cm ulcer with a non-bleeding visible vessel. Second portion normal.
Therapy: dilute epinephrine injection around the vessel, then two hemostatic clips. Good hemostasis.
Impression: duodenal bulb ulcer with non-bleeding visible vessel, treated endoscopically.
Recommendations: high-dose PPI, avoid all NSAIDs, follow biopsy results.
Addendum 12/02: gastric biopsies negative for Helicobacter pylori.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Discharge Summary
Admitted 11/28/2024, discharged 12/01/2024.
Diagnosis: acute upper GI hemorrhage from a duodenal bulb ulcer, NSAID-associated, H. pylori negative.

Course: Hemoglobin 9.4 on arrival, 8.3 the next morning; transfused 1 unit packed red cells. EGD 11/29 with epinephrine and clips to a visible vessel. No rebleeding. Diet advanced. Tacrolimus and prednisone continued; antihypertensives held on day 1 and resumed day 2 as pressures recovered. Creatinine at baseline.

Discharge medications:
NEW pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily for 8 weeks, then stop if off NSAIDs (review with PCP)
NEW ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily for 3 months
STOP naproxen and all NSAIDs
CONTINUE tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, albuterol as needed
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC.
